title: Ailments, Thresholds, Charms and Immunity in Path of Exile 2
summary: How PoE 2 ailments work: buildup, magnitude, duration, threshold, and the difference between resistance, avoidance and immunity, plus how Charms auto-trigger to keep you safe.
description: A mechanics guide to Path of Exile 2 ailments, ailment thresholds and charm-based immunity: what each ailment does, how defences interact, and how to pick the right Charm per encounter.
imageAlt: A row of Charms that grant ailment mitigation and immunity effects in Path of Exile 2

author: Exile2 Guides Editorial Team

items.title: What is an ailment?
body: An ailment is a temporary status effect applied by hits or damage. Damaging ailments deal damage over time (Bleed, Poison, Ignite); non-damaging ailments change how you act (Chill, Freeze, Shock, Electrocute, Stun).

items.title: What is an ailment threshold?
body: Threshold is the amount of buildup an enemy (or you) must accumulate before an ailment is applied. Player base Ailment Threshold is a fraction of Maximum Life; bosses typically have larger thresholds and therefore resist being afflicted.

items.title: How do Charms work?
body: A Charm is carried in a Belt and auto-triggers when its linked condition occurs (for example becoming Frozen). It consumes Charges, which refill at Wells or by killing monsters. Immunity Charms fully prevent the linked ailment instead of just reducing it.

items.title: Resistance vs immunity?
body: Resistance reduces the magnitude or damage of an ailment but does not stop it applying. Immunity (from a Charm or a keystone) fully prevents the ailment from affecting you. The two are not the same.

sections.title: Ailment taxonomy: damaging vs non-damaging
paragraphs: Ailments in Path of Exile 2 split into two groups. Damaging ailments deal damage over time and have their own damage-dealing rules; non-damaging ailments apply a control or debuff effect without a damage-over-time component.

Damaging ailments are Bleed, Poison and Ignite. Non-damaging ailments are Chill, Freeze, Shock, Electrocute and Stun-related effects. Each appears as an icon in your status bar when active; the icon tells you what is happening and how urgent it is.
bullets: Bleed: physical damage over time, usually from attacks; shows a bleeding icon.
Poison: chaos damage over time that stacks with each application; shows a venom icon.
Ignite: fire damage over time; shows a burning icon.
Chill: slows your action speed by a scaled amount; shows a frost icon.
Freeze: briefly stops actions entirely; shows a frozen icon.
Shock: increases damage taken from hits; shows a lightning icon.
Electrocute: a heavier shock-like stun effect; shows a charged icon.
Stun: interrupts action when the stun meter fills; shows a staggered icon.

sections.title: Threshold, buildup, magnitude and duration
paragraphs: Four concepts govern every ailment. Buildup is the meter that fills as you deal ailment damage; once buildup reaches the target's Threshold, the ailment is applied and the meter resets. Magnitude scales how strong the effect is (for example how much Chill slows you, or how much Ignite damages). Duration is how long the applied ailment lasts.

Threshold is the gate: a target with a high threshold needs more buildup to be afflicted. Player base Ailment Threshold is a portion of Maximum Life, while bosses tend to have much larger thresholds, so the same skills that reliably ail a pack may never stick to a boss.
bullets: Buildup: fills toward the Threshold; reaching it applies the ailment.
Threshold: the target value buildup must meet before the ailment lands.
Magnitude: how severe the effect is once applied (slow %, DoT, etc.).
Duration: how long the ailment remains active before expiring.

sections.title: How players apply ailments to enemies
paragraphs: You apply ailments by dealing the matching damage type with a hit or damage-over-time effect. The chance to apply is governed by ailment chance and the enemy's threshold; enough buildup crosses the threshold and the ailment lands.

Some skills and supports are built specifically to apply ailments (for example bleed supports on attacks, or ignite-from-fire spells). Against bosses, investing in ailment magnitude and threshold-breaking modifiers matters far more than against normal monsters.
bullets: Match the damage type to the ailment you want (fire to Ignite, cold to Chill/Freeze, etc.).
Buildup must reach the target threshold; bosses have higher thresholds.
Magnitude improvements make the effect stronger, not easier to apply.
Check the in-game tooltip for the exact buildup and threshold numbers on a given enemy.

sections.title: Avoiding and mitigating ailments
paragraphs: Defences against ailments are layered, and each layer behaves differently. Resistance lowers the magnitude or damage of an ailment but does not stop it from applying. Reduced Effect and Reduced Duration shrink the ailment's impact or how long it lasts. Avoidance can prevent the ailment from being applied in the first place on a roll.

Immunity is the strongest layer: it fully prevents the linked ailment from affecting you, regardless of buildup. Resistance and immunity are not interchangeable - capping fire resistance will not stop you being Ignited, it only reduces the burn.
bullets: Resistance: reduces magnitude/damage, ailment can still apply.
Reduced Effect / Reduced Duration: shrinks or shortens the ailment.
Avoidance: chance to prevent application entirely.
Immunity: fully prevents the linked ailment (Charm or keystone).

sections.title: Charm basics
paragraphs: A Charm is a trinket carried in a Belt that watches for a specific condition and fires automatically when that condition occurs. An Immunity Charm triggers and fully prevents the linked ailment; a Resistance Charm instead grants a temporary resistance boost when its trigger hits.

Each Charm consumes Charges when it triggers. Charges are stored only while the Charm is in a Belt, and they refill at Wells or by killing monsters. A Belt provides a limited number of Charm sockets, so you cannot equip every Charm at once - choose by the content you are running.
bullets: Auto-trigger: fires the moment its linked condition happens.
Charges: consumed on use; refill at Wells or by kills.
Belt sockets: a limited number of Charm slots (see in-game Belt tooltip).
Immunity vs resistance: immunity prevents, resistance only reduces.

sections.title: Which Charm should I use right now?
sections.intro: Pick the situation you expect. The tool points to the Charm that fits and what to watch for.

rules.title: Use a Thawing or Sapphire Charm
steps: Equip a Thawing Charm for full Freeze immunity if freezes are killing you.
Use a Sapphire Charm for a temporary cold-resistance bump if freezes are rare.
Watch your Charm charges - a frozen state with no charges will not clear.

rules.title: Use a Staunching or Antidote Charm
steps: Equip a Staunching Charm to become Immune to Bleeding.
Equip an Antidote Charm to become Immune to Poison.
Prefer immunity Charms over resistance here, since DoT ignores magnitude scaling.

rules.title: Use a Grounding Charm
steps: Equip a Grounding Charm for Shock immunity.
Also consider a Topaz Charm if you only need a resistance bump.
Keep charges topped by killing monsters between packs.

rules.title: Use a Dousing Charm
steps: Equip a Dousing Charm for Ignite immunity.
A Ruby Charm works if you only want fire resistance.
Check the Belt socket count before committing to multiple Charms.

rules.title: Use a Stone Charm
steps: Equip a Stone Charm for Cannot be Stunned while it is active.
Raise your Stun Threshold through gear and passive nodes as a second layer.
Refill charges at Wells before tough bosses.

defaultResult.title: General charm advice
steps: Match the Charm to the most lethal ailment in the content you are running.
Prioritise Immunity Charms for ailments that instantly kill or lock you out.
Refill charges at Wells or by killing monsters before each dangerous encounter.

sections.title: Status icon gallery
sections.intro: Quick reference for the icons you will see on your status bar and on Charms in your Belt.

cards.title: Bleed icon
body: Red droplet. Means physical damage over time is active; counter with a Staunching Charm.

cards.title: Poison icon
body: Green venom. Stacks of chaos damage over time; counter with an Antidote Charm.

cards.title: Ignite icon
body: Orange flame. Fire damage over time; counter with a Dousing Charm.

cards.title: Chill / Freeze icon
body: Blue frost. Slow or full stop; counter with a Sapphire or Thawing Charm.

cards.title: Shock / Electrocute icon
body: Yellow bolt. Increased damage taken or stun; counter with a Grounding Charm.

cards.title: Thawing Charm
body: Grants Immune to Freeze when you become Frozen. Consumes 40 of 40 charges.

cards.title: Staunching Charm
body: Grants Immune to Bleeding when you start Bleeding. Consumes 30 of 40 charges.

cards.title: Antidote Charm
body: Grants Immune to Poison when you become Poisoned. Consumes 20 of 40 charges.

cards.title: Dousing Charm
body: Grants Immune to Ignite when you become Ignited. Consumes 30 of 40 charges.

cards.title: Grounding Charm
body: Grants Immune to Shock when you become Shocked. Consumes 30 of 40 charges.

cards.title: Stone Charm
body: Cannot be Stunned while active. Consumes 20 of 40 charges.

cards.title: Elemental-resistance Charms
body: Ruby, Sapphire, Topaz and Amethyst grant a temporary resistance bump when their damage type hits.

sections.title: Bosses vs players: ailment difficulty
paragraphs: Bosses are meaningfully harder to afflict than regular monsters. Their larger ailment thresholds mean more buildup is required, and many boss fights are tuned so that ailments that trivialise trash mobs barely register.

Because of this, avoid claiming a boss is fully immune or fully controllable unless a current source confirms it. Treat boss ailment application as possible-but-difficult, and verify specific cases against the live client rather than assuming.
bullets: Boss thresholds are larger, so buildup often falls short.
Some bosses resist or shrug off certain ailments by design.
Do not state absolute 'immune' or 'controllable' claims without a current source.
Verify boss-specific ailment behaviour in-game before relying on it.

sections.title: Community evidence and common confusion
sections.intro: Answers to the most repeated player questions about Charms and immunity, drawn from community discussion.

cards.title: Charm equipped but still frozen
body: Usually means no charges left, the wrong Charm for the ailment, the Belt not socketed, or the content disallows Charms. Check charges and the Belt socket first.

cards.title: Resistance is not immunity
body: High fire resistance lowers Ignite damage but does not stop Ignite applying. Only an Immunity Charm or keystone prevents it.

cards.title: Charm did not trigger in time
body: Charges refill at Wells or by kills. Entering a boss with an empty Charm does nothing until it refills.

cards.title: Boss never gets bleeding
body: The boss threshold is high; the same bleed that wrecks a pack may never cross it. Invest in magnitude and threshold-breaking mods, or accept it may not stick.

entries.takeaway: Match your defence layer to the ailment: use Resistance Charms to reduce, Immunity Charms to fully prevent, and keep Charm charges topped before tough fights.

sections.title: Troubleshooting: why your defence failed
paragraphs: When an ailment still hurts you despite preparation, the cause is almost always one of a few repeatable mistakes rather than a hidden mechanic.
bullets: No charges: the Charm was empty because you skipped Wells or kills before the fight.
Wrong Charm: a Sapphire Charm only helps cold damage; it will not stop a Bleed.
Belt not socketed: Charms only hold charges and trigger while in a Belt socket.
Content disallows Charms: some encounters disable trinket auto-effects; plan a passive defence instead.
Confusing resistance with immunity: capping a resistance still lets the ailment apply.

items.question: Do Charms work without a Belt?
answer: No. A Charm can only hold charges and auto-trigger while slotted into a Belt. Without a Belt socket it does nothing.

items.question: Why did my Thawing Charm not stop the freeze?
answer: Most likely it had no charges, was not socketed in your Belt, or the content disables Charm effects. Check charges at a Well before the fight.

items.question: Is 75% fire resistance the same as Ignite immunity?
answer: No. Resistance reduces Ignite damage but the ailment still applies. Only an Immunity Charm or a keystone fully prevents Ignite.

items.question: Can I apply Bleed to every boss?
answer: Not reliably. Bosses have high ailment thresholds, so Bleed may never cross the threshold. Invest in magnitude and threshold-breaking modifiers, and verify in-game.

items.question: How do Charm charges refill?
answer: Charges refill at Wells or by killing monsters. Plan to top up between packs and before boss encounters.

items.question: How many Charms can I equip?
answer: A Belt provides a limited number of Charm sockets; the exact count depends on the Belt. Check the in-game Belt tooltip for your socket total.
